### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

This is a follow-up to #37983, which tracks the same attention-semantics issue in the `VisionTritonAttention` path.

`VisionFlash4Attention` should preserve MiMo-style vision attention semantics when the multimodal attention backend is set to `fa4`. However, the FA4 vision wrapper can drop the `window_size` and `s_aux` / attention sinks kwargs before calling the FlashAttention-4 varlen function.

For vision models whose ViT blocks rely on local-window attention and learned attention sinks, this silently changes the attention semantics when `fa4` is used as the multimodal/vision attention backend. The model can still start and run, but the visual features may be computed without the intended local-window mask and without learned sinks, which can lead to degraded or incorrect multimodal outputs.

The relevant path is:

- `VisionAttention.forward()` receives model-specific vision kwargs such as `window_size` and optional `s_aux`.
- `VisionFlash4Attention.forward()` should extract those kwargs.
- The FA4 wrapper should pass `window_size=...` and, when present, `sinks=s_aux` to `flash_attn_func(..., ver=4)`.

This should be consistent with the FlashAttention3 vision path, which already preserves these kwargs, and with the intended fix direction in #37983 for the Triton backend.

### Reproduction

Reproduction requires a MiMo-style vision model whose ViT blocks use local-window attention and learned attention sinks.

Example launch pattern:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path <model_path> \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --attention-backend triton \
  --mm-attention-backend fa4
```

Then send an image request to the OpenAI-compatible chat completion endpoint:

```python
import requests

payload = {
    "model": "<model_path>",
    "messages": [
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image."},
                {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "<image_url_or_data_url>"}},
            ],
        }
    ],
    "max_tokens": 128,
}

r = requests.post("http://localhost:30000/v1/chat/completions", json=payload)
print(r.status_code)
print(r.text)
```

Actual result:

The server can run, but the FA4 vision attention path may compute attention without preserving the model-provided local-window and sink semantics.

Expected result:

The FA4 vision attention path should preserve the same `window_size` and sink semantics as the model provides, by forwarding:

- `window_size=kwargs.get("window_size", (-1, -1))`
- `sinks=kwargs["s_aux"]` when `s_aux` is present
- `ver=4` for the FA4 kernel path

The fix PR should also include a lightweight unit test for the wrapper behavior. A good regression test would monkeypatch `flash_attn_func`, call `VisionFlash4Attention.forward()` with `window_size` and `s_aux`, and assert that the captured call receives `window_size`, `sinks`, and `ver=4`. This guards the exact silent failure mode without requiring a full model launch in CI.

### Environment

- SGLang version: main / v0.5.18
- Backend: `fa4` for multimodal vision attention
- GPU: NVIDIA B40 / Blackwell
- CUDA: CUDA 13.x environment on Blackwell
- Python: 3.12
- OS: Linux

### Additional context

I locally tested a patch that forwards `window_size` and optional `s_aux` to `flash_attn_func(..., ver=4)`. With this patch, MiMo-V2.5 produced normal multimodal outputs on a Blackwell GPU environment using the FA4 vision backend. I also ran compatibility checks on Qwen3-4B, Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct, and Qwen3.5-4B: all could start with the patched FA4 path, text requests worked, and the VL models handled image requests correctly when using sufficient context length.
title: [Bug] VisionFlash4Attention drops MiMo-style window attention and sinks
